Title: Diagnosis
Details: The provided test `testCalendarTimezoneRespected` fails because the FastDateFormat's format method does not respect the time zone of the Calendar instance passed to it, specifically when formatting the timezone pattern "z". The test constructs a Calendar instance with a timezone different from the system default and expects the formatted string from FastDateFormat to reflect that timezone. However, the FastDateFormat.format(Calendar) method calls the printer.format(Calendar) method, and likely the printer object inside FastDateFormat ignores the timezone of the passed Calendar object, instead always using the system default timezone when formatting the timezone pattern.

The root cause is that the FastDateFormat's internal formatting logic (in printer.format method) doesn't correctly handle the Calendar's timezone for timezone patterns, resulting in always using the machine default timezone for "z" patterns, even though time calculations themselves honor the calendar timezone.

The current bug report aligns with this diagnosis, as it explicitly says the timezone formatting bug causes FastDateFormat to print the machine's default timezone name ignoring the passed calendar timezone. The test verifies the exact same behavior, expecting the timezone abbreviation for the intended timezone.

There are no directly relevant recent bug reports related to timezone handling; they only mention unrelated bugs.

This diagnosis strongly suggests a bug in how FastDateFormat's printer formats timezone "z" patterns when a Calendar is passed to format, where the calendar's timezone is ignored when determining the timezone string to print.

Next, we want to locate and inspect the printer.format(Calendar) method code to confirm if timezone usage is mishandled and fix that so the timezone string formatting reflects the calendar timezone.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
